summary: Discovery call for PLG quickstart trial. Customer is evaluating Redwood hosted API for time-to-first-token and a path to Dedicated/Private later. Key asks: free credits, quick onboarding, SSO/SAML and SOC2 docs, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and a short benchmark. Agreed next steps: provision trial tenant, share security docs, schedule benchmark session.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll just do quick intros. I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood, with Ravi our SE.
[00:07] Dana: Hi, Dana Morales, CTO at Elysium Systems, nice to meet you.
[00:11] Liam: Liam O'Connor, SRE.
[00:14] Priya: Priya Singh, ML engineer.
[00:18] Maya: Awesome. Goal for today is to understand your evaluation, timelines, constraints, and get you spinning up the quickstart trial if that makes sense. We'll keep it loose -- feel free to interrupt.
[00:30] Dana: Yeah, great. We're exploring hosted first, mainly for speed to test. Long term could be dedicated or private if we get to enterprise. Main concerns: latency, cost, and compliance.
[00:42] Maya: Totally. Quick question on current stack, what are you using today for models and infra?
[00:47] Priya: We're using a mix: some OpenAI for prototypes, and internal self-hosted Llama-style models for narrow tasks. We're evaluating moving more workloads to an API to reduce infra overhead.
[00:59] Ravi: Got it. When you say latency, what's your target SLAs? p95, p99, single-turn or multi-turn?
[01:07] Priya: For us, typical single-turn chat/assist calls should be under 300ms p95 for short prompts (under 1k tokens). For longer generation it's okay to be higher but cost matters.
[01:18] Liam: Also need to know about VPC/private later, and auth like SSO/SAML — we have strict onboarding for production.
[01:25] Maya: Makes sense. On hosted quickstart we offer free credits, and the quickstart is usually minutes to first token. We can provision a trial tenant with preloaded credits and a guide; time-to-first-token is often under 10 minutes for simple API calls.
[01:40] Dana: Nice. How do you handle data retention and logs on hosted? We need audit logs for demos.
[01:47] Maya: By default hosted keeps traces for diagnostics, but we have options for shorter retention, and for enterprise we support Private or Dedicated with no telemetry to Redwood's cloud and customer-managed logging. We'll share SOC2 / compliance docs.
[02:02] Priya: Can you zoom into the difference between Dedicated and Private? I always mix those up.
[02:07] Ravi: Sure — Dedicated is reserved, tenant-isolated GPU pools in our infra with guaranteed throughput and SLA. Private typically means VPC or on-prem deployment where control plane is private to the customer, and you manage the networking and KMS.
[02:21] Priya: And pricing differences?
[02:23] Maya: Dedicated is contract-based reserved capacity with monthly commits; Private is more of a licensing/support model since it's customer-managed infra. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing and is fastest to test.
[02:36] Dana: For the quickstart, what do we need to share to get started?
[02:40] Maya: We'll need an admin email to invite, and we'll provision the trial tenant. We'll also give you a quickstart repo and a Postman/cURL example. Typically you can hit tokens within minutes once the key is generated.
[02:52] Liam: Any gotchas for corp network? We have outbound proxies and egress filters.
[02:56] Ravi: If you're behind a proxy you can still call the hosted API; sometimes teams need to whitelist our IP ranges — we'll share that. For secure setups we can demo a connector or suggest using a bastion if needed.
[03:09] Priya: About model options — do you host multiple open models? We try different quantization/latency profiles.
[03:14] Maya: Yes, we maintain a model catalog with curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. Also we surface recommended quantization and batching configs for workloads.
[03:24] Priya: For the benchmark, we want to test throughput at 1k req/day and tail latency. Can you run a short perf test or provide a script?
[03:31] Ravi: We can provide a benchmark script and help run it during the POC. We'll want sample prompts and token-length distribution from you.
[03:38] Dana: Security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS — can you provide the docs?
[03:44] Maya: Yes, we'll share a SOC2 summary, SAML/SSO setup docs, and details on KMS/HSM integrations for Private. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via KMS options for an added layer.
[03:57] Liam: What about data egress/ingestion — do tokens ever leave region? We need EU residency for some workloads.
[04:03] Maya: We have region routing and can pin requests to regions; Dedicated and Private give you stronger guarantees on data locality.
[04:11] Priya: Any pitfalls in moving from hosted trial to dedicated? How fast can we migrate?
[04:16] Ravi: We try to keep APIs consistent. Migration time depends on model variants you choose and capacity planning; small POCs can be moved within weeks with a focused rollout.
[04:25] Dana: Do you support function/tool-calling / structured output? We have extraction tasks.
[04:30] Maya: Yes, hosted API supports streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. We also have recommendation tooling for batching/caching to reduce cost for high throughput use cases.
[04:42] Priya: For cost estimates, can you show examples? We have 50k prompts/day at small sizes and some long-form generation.
[04:49] Maya: We'll send a cost calculator template. For hosted it's per-token; you can use our Optimize suggestions to reduce unit cost via batching and KV prefix caching.
[04:58] Dana: What's the typical sequence after the trial?
[05:02] Maya: Usually: 1) trial and bench-mark 2) internal evaluation 3) decide hosted vs Dedicated 4) contract for Dedicated or setup Private. We'll support canary rollouts and A/B tests during transition.
[05:12] Liam: Ok that's helpful.
[05:15] Maya: Any other blockers or stakeholders to loop in?
[05:18] Dana: Legal will want indemnity and data processing addendum — we'll need those docs.
[05:22] Maya: Yep, will include DPA and standard legal materials.
[05:26] Priya: Let's schedule the benchmark session next week, I'll send prompts and expected latencies.
[05:31] Maya: Great. We'll provision the trial and invite you today. Ravi, we'll pair on the benchmark.
[05:36] Ravi: Sounds good.
[05:38] Maya: Quick recap: I'll provision trial with $2k credits and quickstart guide, share SOC2 and SSO docs, Ravi will produce benchmark script, Priya will share prompts. We'll schedule a 30m benchmark next week. Any final Qs?
[05:53] Dana: Nope, thanks.
[05:55] Liam: Thanks all.
[05:57] Maya: Thanks, bye.

Note: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., "Redwood-verified" heard as "red wood verified", speaker label glitch at 03:31), filler words, and small mis-attributions.
